subject: CascadeHealth: eval scope, dataset spec, and scoring criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: CascadeHealth: eval scope, dataset spec, and scoring criteria

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the extremely helpful discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before Marissa/Ben jump in on the technical onboarding: 

Summary of needs
- Goal: Evaluate model candidates on CascadeHealth triage assistant use case (clinical-notes -> triage recommendation + short rationale).
- Data: ~8k de-identified patient notes you can share for an initial pass; representative mix of urgent / routine / follow-up cases.
- Acceptance: high precision on urgent triage, and overall answer quality judged by clinical reviewers.

Redwood recommended approach
1) Eval run on Redwood Private: we can run the eval inside the VPC you requested so raw data never leaves your environment.
2) Candidate models to start with: redwood-13b-quant (low-latency, tuned for instruction-following), llama-2-13b-chat (strong instruction baseline), and a 70B family for a quality upper bound if needed.
3) Prompt+scoring: we’ll use a mix of exact-match rules for discrete triage labels, and a human-annotated quality rubric for free-text rationales (F1 + contextual quality score).

Immediate next steps I propose
- You drop the de-identified sample (3–5% of dataset) into the shared Drive folder (see links & attachments).
- Redwood to run a baseline inference pass and produce: per-example outputs, automatic discrete-label scoring, and a small human-eval pack for your clinical reviewers.
- Marissa will lead the eval scoping and coordinate label schema; Ben will handle data ingestion and the first benchmark run.

Timeline (proposed)
- Tue 5/26: sample dataset uploaded by CascadeHealth
- Wed 5/27: Redwood initial baseline run + artifact delivery
- Thu 5/28: review call to inspect exemplar failures and agree pass/fail criteria

Attachments: dataset spec CSV, model recommendations PDF, and an XLSX benchmark template.

If that works, I’ll lock the kickoff calendar invite and share the Drive link.

Thanks —
Karthik

Subject: Re: CascadeHealth: eval scope, dataset spec, and scoring criteria

Elena —

Great questions. Answers below and a more concrete spec attached. Short answers first: preferred format JSONL, Redwood will run within your VPC and provide an export package that contains only outputs + computed metrics (no raw input text), and the human-eval pack will be ~200 examples by default (we can adjust).

Dataset format (preferred)- JSONL with each line representing one example. Required fields: 
  - id (string)
  - note_text (string)
  - encounter_type (string; outpatient|urgent|inpatient)
  - gold_triage (string; urgent|routine|followup)
  - metadata (optional; json object as string)

If you cannot produce JSONL, the attached CSV spec maps 1:1 to the fields above. Please ensure de-identification of PHI per your compliance process. 

Private eval & data controls- We will perform the run inside the Private deployment you requested (VPC). The export Redwood provides is a zip containing: per-example model outputs (generated text + model choice + token counts), discrete-label scoring CSV, and a human-eval pack (examples + instructions). Redwood’s compliance team will sign a short attestation for the run confirming no raw dataset leaves your VPC; I’ll escalate to Legal and get that in writing before the run.

Scoring rubric (recommendation)
- Discrete triage label: exact-match accuracy + class-balanced recall (urgent class weighted higher). Threshold: urgent precision >= 0.92 on demo sample to pass baseline.
- Rationale quality: three-point rubric for clinical reviewers (0 = incorrect/unsafe, 1 = partially correct, 2 = clear & clinically actionable). We'll report average rationale score and % examples >= 1. 
- Safety flags: automated detection of hallucination patterns (unsupported clinical claims) using a ruleset and token-level anomaly scoring.

Human-eval pack
- ~200 examples sampled stratified by encounter_type and gold_triage.
- Each example will include model outputs for the 3 recommended candidates and a short annotation form (CSV) for your reviewers.

Next steps (who does what)
- Today: Cascade uploads JSONL sample to Drive or S3 (Elena/Dan).
- Mon 5/25: Redwood completes baseline run and shares result package + link to review doc.
- Tue 5/26: Review call (30–45m) — attendees: Elena, Dan, Karthik, Marissa, Ben.

Marissa & Ben: please pick this up on Monday; Ben to confirm the ingestion pipeline (S3 vs Drive) and Marissa to prepare the annotation instructions.

Thanks — feel free to ping me if anything needs faster turnaround.

Karthik
